newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia banks, insurers seen cooperating.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia banks, insurers seen cooperating.

text.p: Slovenian banks and insurers are seen forming a wave of alliances to help them weather an expected increase in foreign competition, the government's Office for Control of Insurers said on Friday.
"We may see more cooperation and possibly some capital link-ups in the future as insurers and banks seek to improve cost and market strategies," Jurij Gorisek, director of the office, told Reuters.

Slovenia's largest insurer Zavarovalnica Triglav and the country's largest bank, state-owned Nova Ljubljanska banka, earlier this week signed a long-term cooperation agreement on the joint introduction of new products and better services.

"The basic reason for the contract is a strategic one: we want to prepare for European competition where small banks and insurers will have poor chances of competing with the bigger ones," said Joze Obersnel, a member of Triglav's management board.
He added that the two companies were in discussions about setting up a joint venture that would offer a combination of banking and insurance services.
Last month, Slovenia's second largest bank SKB formed a joint insurance company with Italian-controlled Austrian insurer EA-Generali.
The joint company, Generali SKB, plans to concentrate on life insurance products for which it expects to get a licence by the end of May.
"The goal of the venture is to expand banking services by introducing new products," said Ivo Bizjak, a member of Generali SKB's management board.
According to Gorisek, various banks hold stakes in four of Slovenia's 12 insurance companies but have so far shied away from setting up joint operations, except in the case of Generali SKB.

Four Slovenian insurers are partially owned by foreign companies but the number of international insurers operating in Slovenia is expected to increase substantially as the country approaches the European Union (EU).
The country signed an EU association agreement in June last year and hopes to become a full member as soon as possible. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
